reviewerErrorAtTurn1.disclosure: I consented at turn 1 with 0 and 0. Codex was right and I was wrong. D157-MF-1 is a real defect that I missed.
reviewerErrorAtTurn1.whatIMissed: The turn-1 row's evidence cell said only 'refused at admission; no ExecutionId'. v1-slice §7 item 8 is disjunctive: an excluded form in a PlanIntent is rejected during request validation and creates no ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, ExecutionPlan or authoritative Run; AND a substitution after admission is also rejected before any stage executes. EE-5b lives wholly in the second fate — v5's pass reads 'Detected substitution is rejected before any stage executes' — and EE-4 carries both. The turn-1 row assigned EE-5b a fate that is not EE-5b's.
reviewerErrorAtTurn1.mechanism: The error originates one review earlier. When I graded the seven-class bundle in preview-product-boundary-admission-leftover.v1, I printed v5's pass conditions truncated at about 110 characters. EE-5b's string was cut at 'If the act is only an ambien' and EE-4's post-admission sentence was cut off entirely. On that truncated evidence I recorded that all seven classes share one property, 'refused at admission or request validation with no ExecutionId'. That statement is false for EE-5b. I then carried the conclusion into my D-157 turn-1 CONSENT without re-reading the source.
reviewerErrorAtTurn1.classOfError: Truncated reading of a primary source — the same defect class I have charged in subjects in this corpus, including a truncated verbatim quotation and a truncated owner cell. My own tooling produced the truncation and I did not notice the ellipsis.
reviewerErrorAtTurn1.correctionNow: I re-read v1-slice §7 item 8 and all seven v5 pass conditions in full before assessing the repair.
reviewerErrorAtTurn1.effectOnMyPriorVerdicts: My ACCEPT of the leftover artifact and my turn-1 CONSENT stand as recorded acts, but the ground I gave for the over-bundling attack in the leftover verdict was partly wrong and should not be relied on. The bundle itself survives on corrected evidence — see bundleStillCoherent — but not for the reason I gave.
reviewerErrorAtTurn1.notOvercorrecting: Having been shown wrong, the temptation is to inflate a finding at turn 2 to look rigorous. I have graded the one new item I found as an advisory on its merits, and I say so explicitly so the coordinator can discount for that bias.

bundleStillCoherent.question: With the fates corrected, do the seven classes still belong at one gate, or does the correction expose the over-bundling I wrongly cleared at the leftover review?
bundleStillCoherent.answer: One gate still holds, on corrected evidence. v1-slice §7 item 8 is a single litmus with two limbs, not two separate laws, and v5's EE-5b applies only where the act carries a request or protocol representation — so every one of the seven is a representation-based excluded-form refusal, differing only in the checkpoint at which the refusal lands. The row now names both checkpoints and both corpora, which is what makes one gate honest rather than convenient.
bundleStillCoherent.confinementNotClaimed: v5's EE-5b also holds that arbitrary ambient acts of an already-running trusted-TCB component are not admission-enforced and are not claimed confined. The turn-2 row uses the word 'represented' three times — in the claim's lead, in the substitution item and in the evidence cell — and that qualifier is exactly what keeps the row from claiming confinement of ambient acts. On the row where I once accepted a false enforcement claim, this is the discipline holding.

coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Fifteen attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Read the disclosure first: I consented at turn 1 with 0 and 0, and Codex was right that the row mis-stated the fates. v1-slice §7 item 8 is disjunctive — an excluded form is rejected in request validation creating no ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, ExecutionPlan or authoritative Run, and a substitution after admission is also rejected before any stage executes. EE-5b lives wholly in the second limb and EE-4 carries both, so the turn-1 cell's 'refused at admission; no ExecutionId' assigned EE-5b a fate that is not EE-5b's. The error started one review earlier: when I graded the seven-class bundle in the leftover artifact I printed v5's pass strings truncated at about 110 characters, so I never saw EE-5b's pre-stage clause, and I carried that conclusion into turn 1 without re-reading. That is the truncated-source defect class I have charged in subjects, produced by my own tooling. Both dispositions land, verified against primary bytes rather than against the disposition table's description of itself. The claim now reads admission and pre-stage validation of represented excluded forms, the harness names both the admission corpus and the substitution-mutation corpus, the evidence cell maps one-to-one onto §7 item 8's two limbs, and item 1, the Why paragraph and item 5 all state the same split. D157-SF-1's phrase landed and tracks v5's EE-1 invariant more closely than what it replaced. Nothing rode in under cover of the repair: the condition-4 operands are byte-identical between turns and the Before operand still occurs exactly once, five of eight row cells are unchanged, the seven-class membership is unchanged, and the prose diff is confined to turn-2 bookkeeping and the two dispositions. I re-tested the bundling question rather than assuming it, and one gate still holds on corrected evidence, because §7 item 8 is one litmus with two limbs and all seven classes are representation-based refusals; the word 'represented', used three times, is what keeps the row from claiming confinement of ambient trusted-TCB acts. The advisory is that the evidence cell keeps only ExecutionId where §7 item 8 and v5's EE-4 name four artifacts; the cell cites the governing section so nothing false is asserted, and I note explicitly that I did not inflate it to compensate for turn 1.
